verses.text: Abram went up from Egypt into the south with his wife, everything he owned, and Lot.
Abram had become very wealthy, with livestock, silver, and gold.
He traveled from the Negev back to Bethel, to the place where his tent had been before, between Bethel and Ai.
He returned to the altar he'd built earlier, and there Abram called on Yahweh's name.
Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.
The land couldn't support them living together because they had so many possessions.
Arguments broke out between Abram's herders and Lot's herders. The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land at that time.
Abram said to Lot, "Please, let's not fight—you and me, or our herders. We're family.
Isn't the whole land open in front of you? Let's separate. If you go left, I'll go right; if you go right, I'll go left."
Lot looked up and saw that the whole Jordan plain was well watered, before Yahweh destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah. It looked like Yahweh's garden and like the land of Egypt, all the way toward Zoar.
So Lot chose the Jordan plain for himself and traveled east. The two of them separated.
Abram stayed in Canaan, while Lot settled in the cities of the plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
The people of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinned greatly against Yahweh.
After Lot had separated from him, Yahweh said to Abram, "Look up from where you are. Look north, south, east, and west.
I'll give you and your descendants all the land you can see, forever.
I'll make your descendants as numerous as the dust of the earth. If anyone could count every speck of dust, then your descendants could be counted too.
Get up and walk through the land, from one end to the other. I'm giving it to you."
Abram moved his tent and settled by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron. He built an altar to Yahweh there.
